title: FHFA House Price Index — Monthly Index (August 2026 data)
source: FHFA: fhfa.gov/data/hpi fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes), the agency's own "FHFA HPI Release Dates" table, whose "2026 HPI Release Dates" block reads "Tuesday, October 27 | Monthly Index | August 2026". The same table carries the surrounding 2026 rows (September 29, November 24, December 29) and the full 2027 schedule (fifteen dated rows, January 26 -> December 28), so this is a forward calendar the publisher maintains rather than a one-off announcement. Promoted estimate -> confirmed by this lane's own independent fetch, on the same precedent the fhfa-hpi-2026-11-24 lane used: the no-self-confirm convention binds the sweep that DISCOVERED an event (new-home-sales-2026-10-27), not its independent second look. UNLIKE the 11-24 sibling this rests on ONE primary and the ledger says so: the second FHFA document that names 11-24 in prose (the published 2026Q2 report's Notes) names September 29 and November 24 and NOT October 27, and the corroborating document for this date is the July-data monthly report that has not been published yet. Structural corroboration instead: 2026-10-27 is the last Tuesday of October 2026, and the archive is 68 of 68 last-Tuesday releases since 2021 (271-row report archive, all 12 paginated pages, 1996-03-21 -> 2026-08-25, fetched 2026-09-06). No release time is stated on the primary and none is claimed here. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: The MONTHLY edition, one month ahead of the quarterly fhfa-hpi-2026-11-24 sibling, and the distinction is the whole reason this ledger exists separately: 2026-10-27 is FOMC DAY 1 of the October 27-28 meeting (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes, fetched 2026-09-06). Because FHFA releases on the last Tuesday and the FOMC meets Tuesday-Wednesday, an FHFA release day can be FOMC day 1 but never day 2 -- measured at 17 of 68 releases since 2021, and ALL 17 are monthly editions (0 of 20 quarterly). This print is the 18th. Impact LOW, symbols empty, and the tape work is the strongest null the family has produced: 36 permutation tests (four release-day subsets x nine housing/broad instruments, 20,000 iterations, session high-low range since 2021) return exactly two hits at p<0.05 -- LEN on all-68 (p=0.0407) and DHI on the monthly-non-FOMC subset (p=0.0269) -- and BOTH are NARROWER on release days, the wrong sign for a "housing print moves housing names" story, against ~1.8 hits expected by chance. PHM's p=0.0443 on the FOMC-day-1 subset dissolves to p=0.0545 against the correct control (the other 28 FOMC day-1 sessions). It reaches no model and no regulator: 0 hits for fhfa/hpi/house price/case-shiller across both sheets of the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx, and the Federal Reserve's own 2026 supervisory stress-test scenario sources its "U.S. House Price Index" variable to the Fed's Z.1 Financial Accounts series FL075035243.Q -- with 0 mentions of FHFA, CoreLogic, Case-Shiller or Zillow anywhere on that page.
